rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill. It has `name`/`description` front matter and is matched by the `skills` site query, so `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.references` applies. The requirement lets a skill link to specialized material, but each such link must say when to read the file. I checked every link in the file:
- `[CI example](references/ci.md)` is introduced by "Use the … when adding these steps to an existing workflow". Setup and review of project CI is the trigger.
- `[references/distributed-requirements.md]` is introduced by "For an obligation that applies separately at each of many sites … read … before drafting it, and whenever you edit a `{req}` that contains `{sites}` or `{violations}`". That names the trigger.
- `[references/syntax-details.md]` is introduced by "If a file that implements or tests a requirement cannot carry a comment, such as a shipped skill or a stylesheet …, or a requirement lives in a nested chapter, read …". That also names the trigger.

The mention of the habeas-evidence skill's `references/fixme.md` is plain code text in another skill's namespace, not a link from this skill. It is also tied to the `{fixme}` reference, so it gives context either way. No violation queries were listed, and I found no link that lacks a stated reading condition. I found no gap.
